Heavy Rains Disrupt Electric Utilities in Kyushu, Operations Resume

A week of record-breaking rainfall across southern Japan has disrupted operations at several electric utilities’ facilities, including those managed by Kyushu Electric Power Co Inc. Torrential rains, which began on June 13 and ended on June 19, triggered flooding and landslides that temporarily cut access to power plants and damaged transmission lines in Kumamoto and Miyazaki prefectures.

Kyushu Electric Power Co Inc reported that floodwaters breached protective barriers at its Hitoyoshi hydroelectric plant on June 15, leading to a precautionary shutdown of turbines and evacuation of staff. “Safety was our utmost priority. We worked closely with local authorities to monitor river levels and secure the site,” said spokesperson Hiroshi Tanaka. The company dispatched emergency repair teams as soon as conditions allowed, restoring limited operations within 48 hours.

Meanwhile, another operator, Satsuma Power Holdings, faced delays in coal deliveries to its Sendai thermal plant after landslides blocked key railway routes. According to the Kyushu Electric Utility Workers’ Union, over 150 personnel were deployed to clear debris and inspect infrastructure for damage before resuming normal operations on June 20.

The Kyushu Electric Power Industry Association estimates that the outages and slowdowns affected up to 3% of the region’s total power generation capacity at the peak of the disruption. “Thanks to coordinated efforts, all affected facilities are now back online and supplying electricity as usual,” said association chairperson Keiko Fujimoto. Experts note that while infrastructure proved resilient, continued vigilance is needed as extreme weather events become more frequent.
